Messages.Author: Iain Paisley
Messages.Body:
It seems to me that the fight over card limits has become somewhat heated.
It reminds me of the religious strife in many countries, including my own
(Ulster). I have noted many similarities between the religious
fundamentalists and the people who post to this group. On both sides there
has been signs of the basic principle that keeps religious factions at war;
the inability to accept the full merits of the other side of the argument
and a plain lack of respect for anyone who posts on the said matter before
you have even read what they have had to say for themselves. No I suspect
that this last statement will call for lots of replys, saying "It wasn't
Me!", "It was all the NL/CL players's fault", "They started it". Now, before
you put the metaphorical pen to paper let me remind you that no matter how
flowery your writing, no matter how clever your wording you can't escape
this basic fact. So think first, before you make yourselves sound even more
petty.

When it comes to religion, I, personally, rejoice in the mighty variety of
faiths under gods eye. We may have our differences, but we all agree of the
fundamental basics. It is the same with Jyhad (or V:tES, for any of you new
agers). There is a huge variety of ways to play the game; NL, NL+GT, 3CL,
4CL, 5CL, 6CL and any of the above with 1CL on uniques added, and all of
these games has its own slight differences of style of play and deck
building. People presumably play the game that they best prefer (if not then
this comes to a different matter entirely, so please don't pick me up on
this minor point and waste the rest of the message). Like religion there
will always be people calling for the game to be standardised to increase
its popularity, but I say the opposite - standardising could alienate the
players who prefer the style that becomes non-standard (perhaps sub-standard
in many peoples minds), just like with religions. I think that it would
probably be best to acknowledge the great variety that the game has to
offer, and credit all of the possible styles with a fully unbiased account
of each way of playing the game, so that WotC could publish it fully and
allow people, with the free will that God has given them, to make up their
own minds. I think that the rulebook, like the bible, is deliberately vague
(on this matter at least - other matters are of no concern here). WotC seems
to have been non-commital on this account, I suspect for the same reasons
that I am putting forward here. It is surely true that they don't discount
any style when considering new cards - how, for instance did both Archon
Investigation (Essential for a fair CL game) and Corruption (Useful only in
an NL game) come to be printed. I also think that there needs to be a
distinction, when considering any merits of all styles of play, between
tournament types and social game types of play.

I would personally like someone compile a definitive, unbiased, account of
the merits of every type of game, for all to view and comprehend - who knows
maybe there will be a definate outcome in favour of one style, but I doubt
it. But until this is produced (By a combination of NL and CL players,
hopefully) any criticism of either style would seem pure speculation - as
everyone with the inclination to argue has already a biased opinion one way
or the other.

I will look forward to the day when people will KNOW the true differences
between CL and NL.

Thankyou for your time,

Annonymous

Messages.Author: Malcolm McCallum
Messages.Body:
I'd like to think my groups reasons for playing CL or NCL are in fact
reasons and not just dogma. Of course, we began playing with a 4CL
because Jyhad had that limit. Yes S&B was a problem. Our group's solution
was to shame people out of using it as a no-brainer strategy. Similarily,
we had to shame people out of building Misdirection decks.

With V:TES, there was NCL. Rumours floated around about a restricted list
and we generally incorporated that. Restricting potentially abusive cards
to a limit of 2. We stuck with the 4CL though because we felt it was not
in any way crippling, or preventing us from making interesting decks. We
had to make decks though that could never be focussed on a single card or
pair of cards.

To our minds, if we went to NCL, we would be opening ourselves up to
obscene decks on a regular basis. It isn't the core group that we would
worry about but the fringe player who would bring a monster to the table
once in awhile.

Recently we moved up to a 6CL as a way of experimenting, and removed the
restricted list. Generally, most people just tossed a couple more cards
into their old decks. Since doing it though we've seen a Ventrue tribe
out with 6 blood dolls, another deck drop a misdirection every turn for 6
turns, and decks that WWEF 2 and 3 times a turn.

We are going back to 4CL for the most part. Again it is being done by
shame though. I'm not getting any flak for having 6 Corruption cards in
my Settite deck..yet, but most of us are just shaking our heads over the
decks we see in a 6CL. Logic tells us that a NCL would be more obscene.

I think there is a sort of religion in all this though. It is that our
group plays for the amusement and the interesting variations that we see.
We've generally got no interest in tournaments or trying to win in an
aggressive NCL environment. We prefer to walk away from the table when
someone drops decks that are not fun to play against. CL and NCL are just
a common focus for the schism. I think the religious differences are
between those that go for the throat and enjoy having their throat gone
for, and those others that aim for a kindler, gentler environment.

Messages.Author: Algustas
Messages.Body:
Hi Errol,

On 25 Oct 1996, Errol T wrote:

> Until I start reading in the paper how people are killing each other over
> Vampire like fanatics do over Religion then do even compare them in the
> same sentence.
>

Well, there are some definate similarities though. Let's look at them.

1) There is a debate between one side that uses logical argument,
and another side that uses passionate argument.

2) One sides stand is based on history (that's the way we did it
in m****) and one sides stand is based on changing conditions of a new game.

3) One side listens to the other sides arguments, then logically
refutes it. The other side pretends to listen to the arguments, then
ignores them and starts in with a fresh new passionate argument.

4) While some people claim we should agree to disagree, that is
just about as likely as Martin Luther (the original) agreeing to disagree
with the Catholic church...

Seems like a pretty good comparrison to me...
Algustas

*****The opinions that are held with passion are always those for which
no good ground exists; indeed the passion is the measure of the holder's
lack of rational conviction. Opinions in politics and religion are almost
always held passionately.***** Bertrand Russel

Messages.Author: theCorrupter
Messages.Body:
On Tue, 22 Oct 1996, Iain Paisley wrote:

> It seems to me that the fight over card limits has become somewhat heated.

It seems to be one of those things. I was here since the beginning of the
group (albeit as a lurker then), and roughly every 2 to 3 months, the
CL-NL debates heat up again. Usually they end in either, "let's agree to
disagree" or with people heatedly leaving the newsgroup. Unfortunatly, I
know of many good players who have left reading/contributing to this group
(on both side of the NL/CL fence) because they were sick of hearing about
it.

> It reminds me of the religious strife in many countries, including my own
> (Ulster). I have noted many similarities between the religious > fundamentalists and the people who post to this group. On both sides there
> has been signs of the basic principle that keeps religious factions at war;
> the inability to accept the full merits of the other side of the argument
> and a plain lack of respect for anyone who posts on the said matter before
> you have even read what they have had to say for themselves.

I would welcome anyone to look at my posts via DejaNews (www.dejanews.com)
and look for an example where I _ever_ do this. When I do, I _always_
apologize, but it just isn't something that typically happens. While in
previous CL debates, I recall CL-supporters who did the same, the current
one seems to have CL-supporters of the ilk you describe, with few
exceptions.

> No I suspect
> that this last statement will call for lots of replys, saying "It wasn't
> Me!", "It was all the NL/CL players's fault", "They started it". Now, before
> you put the metaphorical pen to paper let me remind you that no matter how
> flowery your writing, no matter how clever your wording you can't escape
> this basic fact. So think first, before you make yourselves sound even more
> petty.

I don't mind sounding petty. :)

<TOPIC=OFF>
For anyone reading this, I always welcome comments, criticism, etc., for
anything I might write. There is a reason I have the line
"...Comments?.." in my .sig. Use it if you think it's necessary...
</TOPIC>

> When it comes to religion, I, personally, rejoice in the mighty variety of
> faiths under gods eye. We may have our differences, but we all agree of the
> fundamental basics.

And even if we disagree on the basics (atheism v. monotheism v. polytheism
v etc...), we should still respect each others opinions. However, I do
have a problem with antagonistic street preachers in my own town of
Madison. I _don't_ like how they attack those of different views _and_
avoid debate. I don't mind being challenged, but I want it to be honest
_interaction_ and not simply a beleaguered bunch of dogma. As I said
above (and I do apologize for the harshness of it, but I prefer brutal
honesty), I feel that currently all that I hear from the CLers is dogma.
As L. Scott said, rebuttal has been : "Stop countering my points! YOU
aren't listening..."

> It is the same with Jyhad (or V:tES, for any of you new
> agers). There is a huge variety of ways to play the game; NL, NL+GT, 3CL,
> 4CL, 5CL, 6CL and any of the above with 1CL on uniques added, and all of
> these games has its own slight differences of style of play and deck
> building.

Quite.

> People presumably play the game that they best prefer (if not then
> this comes to a different matter entirely, so please don't pick me up on
> this minor point and waste the rest of the message).

Prefer implies that they know the alternatives. For many people with any
of the above styles, this may not be the case.

> Like religion there
> will always be people calling for the game to be standardised to increase
> its popularity, but I say the opposite - standardising could alienate the
> players who prefer the style that becomes non-standard (perhaps sub-standard
> in many peoples minds), just like with religions.

While you could alienate those players who are on the other side of the
fence, the game's future fan-base will be more secure. There is something
telling about going to conventions and having people say to you, "Oh,
Jyhad. It's broken". These people all played some varying variety of
"Jyhad" that was usually nothing like other players' games. When I've run
tourneys outside of Madison, support was minimal. Usually those few
players who were interested (20-40) dwindled down to 10-20 because it
wasn't the way they were used to playing (some old-DCI, some pure-NL, some
4CL, some old-old-DCI, some this some that some etc...), and they thought
it wouldn't work and would support Killer Deck X (usually some Bleed deck
complaint). The winners of those two tournaments, however, were a
LifeBoon deck that actually withdrew (!!!) to win the finals, and an
Apathy,blockbadstuffandrunawayfromcombatandeventuallybleedwithachingly
beautifulvampiresagainandagainwhocaresifyougetblockedthey'realmostdead
deck.

Alienating players already happens now. With a decisive standard
(something Robert Goudie and I were working on, and I hope have finally
made a decisive impact on), people who start the game stay with the game
and aren't turned away later on.

> I think that it would
> probably be best to acknowledge the great variety that the game has to
> offer, and credit all of the possible styles with a fully unbiased account
> of each way of playing the game, so that WotC could publish it fully and
> allow people, with the free will that God has given them, to make up their

> (on this matter at least - other matters are of no concern here). WotC seems
> to have been non-commital on this account, I suspect for the same reasons
> that I am putting forward here. It is surely true that they don't discount
> any style when considering new cards - how, for instance did both Archon
> Investigation (Essential for a fair CL game)

<Aside>
Archon Investigation is only "essential" in CL because CL makes Malk S&B
so nasty that they need a card that is broken to destroy the brokenness of
the strategy in that environment. Note that Malk S&B is one of the only
strategies _totally_ unencumbered by CL. (Need reference? Judith and
Mark's Jyhad page, link available from my .sig).

AI, is IMHO, a Magic-card. As a single card that destroys a strategy
(built up bleed strategy), it shouldn't have been printed.
</Aside>

> and Corruption (Useful only in
> an NL game) come to be printed. I also think that there needs to be a
> distinction, when considering any merits of all styles of play, between
> tournament types and social game types of play.

What is the distinction you suggest?

> I would personally like someone compile a definitive, unbiased, account of
> the merits of every type of game, for all to view and comprehend - who knows
> maybe there will be a definate outcome in favour of one style, but I doubt
> it. But until this is produced (By a combination of NL and CL players,
> hopefully) any criticism of either style would seem pure speculation - as
> everyone with the inclination to argue has already a biased opinion one way
> or the other.

Thomas Doehne has offered to start it. I'll house it on my page or
contribute, as needed. I had long been considering something of this sort
myself, but haven't taken the time.

> I will look forward to the day when people will KNOW the true differences
> between CL and NL.

I would amend this to "when MORE people will know...". Currently, I think
there are a lot of people who do (R. Garfield being one of them. He plays
NL-Jyhad, BTW) (Sorry, just had to throw in a cheap, meaningless comment
to get jumped on! ;)
